correctness.summary: An explicit family of star coordinates gives the stated upper bound. For the lower bound, one distance-two pair from each non-singleton part requires a distinct tree coordinate by the four-point condition. If at least two singleton parts exist, using only those coordinates collapses both singleton vertices to the unique midpoint in every coordinate, forcing one additional coordinate.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The September 2026 graph-phylogenetic-rank paper separately gives the complete-bipartite and perfect-matching-complement cases and asks for bounded-rank structure, but does not state the general complete-multipartite formula. Speyer--Sturmfels gives the underlying max-mixture research problem. Cartwright--Chan's adjacent complete-multipartite cover theorem uses an explicitly different tree-rank convention. Exact and synonymous searches did not locate equivalent prior coverage; differently named older metric-decomposition results and very recent parallel work remain residual risks.

value.summary: The theorem gives an exact formula on all connected complete multipartite graphs, unifies several separately known examples, identifies the singleton correction mechanism, and completely characterizes bounded phylogenetic rank inside this natural graph family.

limitations: The theorem is restricted to connected complete multipartite graph metrics.
It does not characterize arbitrary graphs of bounded phylogenetic rank.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; differently named older metric-decomposition results or very recent parallel work remain residual risks.
